reading.body:
H.R. 6984, the Data Center Transparency Act, is a Democratic-led bill whose recorded support is almost entirely from one party, with two Republican cosponsors.

The sponsor is Robert Menendez and there are fifteen cosponsors, fourteen Democrats and two Republicans, Brian Fitzpatrick and Michael Lawler. The bill's own text is tagged with two issues, energy and data centers. That pairing is the substance: this is legislation aimed at the physical layer of AI, the buildings and the power they draw, rather than at models or data.

Four lobbying filings from 2025 or later name the bill. The filers are the American Federation of Teachers with two filings, Google Client Services, and the Santa Clara Valley Water District. A filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it, so these three do not tell you whether any of them supports or opposes the measure. The presence of a water district alongside a technology company is the notable fact, and it is consistent with a bill about data centers rather than about AI software.

What the data does not cover is the bill's content, its committee stage, any vote, or its prospects. It records a latest status date of 2026-01-08 and nothing about what happened on it. The cosponsor list is a snapshot from LegiScan, and the lobbying count is limited to filings from 2025 onward, so earlier activity would not appear.

summary: H.R. 6984, Data Center Transparency Act. Latest status date 2026-01-08. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: energy and data centers. 4 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
